title: status readers B1: review derivation via in-process gix (zero subprocess on the status path)
action: Port ONLY the review-derivation half of the status read spine and remove its subprocess cost (D5 headline; split from the recovery/state half per panel W8, which is now rust-port-20): listCandidates, listReviews, deriveCandidateStatus (reviews.mjs:117/362/483) and the unreviewed/in-review/reviewed/stale classification incl. high_risk_unreviewed. The two git questions node answers by spawning (reviews.mjs:401 merge-base --is-ancestor and rev-list --count) are answered IN-PROCESS with gix — no subprocess on the status path — keeping node's per-pass memo semantics (same head/ref pair asked once) and node's fail-open contract: an unreadable repo, missing ref, or gix error degrades the whole review block exactly as node's try/catch does (degraded flag), never a silent wrong count. TRI-STATE FIDELITY: node reads `merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 0/1/other (reviews.mjs:428-435) — an unknown/missing object maps to UNRESOLVED, never to covered:false; reproduce that three-way distinction, do not collapse it. GIX RECORD AND ESCAPE HATCH: recorded in approach.md:18-21 (libgit2 rejected for musl/D8); approach.md:21's condition is honored — if the gix query set does not measure under 2ms on this repo, front it with the mtime-keyed cache described there rather than reverting to spawn. Adding gix to crates/bee-core/Cargo.toml plus the crates/Cargo.lock consequence is IN SCOPE; if the crates.io fetch is unavailable, return [BLOCKED] — never vendor ad hoc. PANIC DISCIPLINE (panel B4, and rust-port-18 is the profile fix): the gix path must be panic-free by construction — no unwrap/expect/slice-index on untrusted repo data — and carries a malformed-repo PANIC-PROBE fixture proving a corrupt/truncated object store degrades the review block instead of aborting the process. DIVERGENCE-CLASS FIXTURES, each named (panel W5): shallow clone (git CLI exits 0 with a truncated count — rust must not silently disagree), packed-refs-only, detached HEAD, linked worktree HEAD, objects/info/alternates, commit-graph present, refs/replace or grafts, and unknown-object is-ancestor. Git-dependent fixtures use the grown generator's git-initialized roots (rust-port-19) with real ancestry; assert NON-TRIVIALITY — the node oracle produced real NON-degraded counts on the primary fixture — plus a separate degraded-parity fixture. ALL tests in ONE target status_readers_b1.

prohibitions: No edits to .bee/bin/ or packages/bee/ (D1 freeze)
No git subprocess on the status path (gix in-process only) — the whole point of this cell
No unwrap/expect/index on untrusted repo data
No ad-hoc vendoring if crates.io is unavailable — return [BLOCKED]

Tests never touch the live .bee/ store

trace.outcome: Ported the review-derivation half of the status read spine to bee_core::reviews with both git questions answered in process by gix (D5 headline: zero subprocess on the status path). Tri-state is-ancestor preserved (unknown object -> unresolved -> 'review stale'/'range unresolvable', never covered:false); JS coercion semantics reproduced bug-for-bug so memo keys and fail-open behavior match mjs; panic-free on untrusted repo data plus catch_unwind as the faithful port of buildReviewBlock's try/catch. gix pinned default-features=false (no network transports, no C deps) to keep musl/D8 viable. Two real divergences found and fixed by the fixtures: gix 0.86 loads no refs/replace table by default (inverted core.useReplaceRefs condition) and the walk-based is-ancestor fallback proved unreachable and was removed as dead code. approach.md:21's under-2ms condition was NOT met by the bare query set (12-15ms release on this repo, 971 commits), so its named escape hatch is implemented: an mtime-keyed cache fronts the query set (1.6-1.8ms hot, still zero subprocess), cached only for definite answers and object-id specs, keyed on resolved HEAD + shallow + replace + alternates so a stale hit is impossible.
